description.value: The study examined relations between cognitive and motor deficits and regional gray matter volumes in individuals with alcohol dependence compared with healthy controls.

spans.text: Relations between cognitive and motor deficits and regional brain volumes in individuals with alcoholism

description.value: Cross-sectional comparison of individuals with alcohol dependence and healthy controls.

spans.text: This study extends previous research by directly comparing nonamnesic alcoholics across several functional domains in relation to cortical and subcortical brain volumes.
The ALC and CTRL groups
ALC
No alcoholic participant had ever been diagnosed with Wernicke’s encephalopathy
CTRL
No control participant met DSM-IV-TR criteria for substance abuse or dependence.

name.value: ALC had smaller regional brain volumes than CTRL

spans.text: ALC had smaller cingulate [t(129)=2.36, p=.020, Cohen’s d=.42, 3.5% smaller], insular [t(129)=2.84, p=.005, Cohen’s d=.42, 4% smaller], parietal [t(129)=2.39, p=.018, Cohen’s d=.42, 3% smaller], and hippocampal [t(127)=2.16, p=.033, Cohen’s d=.38, 3.5% smaller] volumes and modestly smaller frontal [t(129)=1.96, p=.052, Cohen’s d=.35, 2% smaller] volumes than CTRL ( Table 3 ).

Based on our hypotheses we also measured subcortical and cerebellar regions including the caudate, pons, hippocampus, thalamus, and superior cerebellum.

This study demonstrated that the alcoholics examined herein had volume deficits in frontal, cingulate, insular, parietal, and hippocampal regions.

spans.text: #### Correlations Between Functional Composite Scores and Regional Brain Volumes in ALC

definition.value: Lower EF scores correlated with smaller frontal, temporal, and insular volumes in ALC

spans.text: Lower EF scores correlated with smaller frontal (r=.20, p=.036), temporal (r=.26, p=.008), and insular (r=.24, p=.014) volumes ( Table 4 ).
Lower EF scores correlated with smaller frontal (r=.20, p=.036), temporal (r=.26, p=.008), and insular (r=.24, p=.014) volumes ( Table 4 ).

Use of False Discovery Rates (FDR: based on 3 comparisons across the cognitive and motor domains; p≤.0167/.033/.05) reduced the risk of reporting false positive results ( Benjamini and Hochberg 1995 ).

Correlational analyses (Pearson product-moment) tested relations between composite scores and brain volumes and relations among these measures and alcohol or demographic variables within the ALC group.
Lower EF scores correlated with smaller frontal (r=.20, p=.036), temporal (r=.26, p=.008), and insular (r=.24, p=.014) volumes ( Table 4 ).

value: Lower EF scores correlated with smaller frontal, temporal, and insular volumes.
